extracted.intended_audience: educators, researchers, developers, and potential grantees/partners in educational technology and education research
extracted.subtask_description: Describes Chan Zuckerberg Initiative / Learning Commons priorities and standards for supporting and building education research, edtech products, and open infrastructure. Useful for prospective grantees, partners, and collaborators seeking to align proposals or projects with CZI's education goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand access to effective teaching and learning practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning Commons aims to expand access to effective teaching and learning practices — so that every learner has the opportunity to thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority on scalability and equitable access: projects should demonstrate they expand reach of practices that are known to be effective and contribute to improved opportunities for diverse learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared, open infrastructure built for the public good
rubrics_metrics.description: Through shared, open infrastructure built for the public good, Learning Commons aims to expand access of effective teaching and learning practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor open, interoperable platforms and resources intended as public goods rather than proprietary, closed systems; emphasis on shared infrastructure that others can adopt or build on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring learning science into everyday tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Our mission is to bring learning science into the tools used every day by teachers and students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects and products should embed evidence-based principles from learning science directly into commonly used educational tools, not just as separate research artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary collaboration among educators, researchers, and developers
rubrics_metrics.description: That is why we’re bringing together educators, researchers, and developers to build open, research-driven technology...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support work that meaningfully involves practitioners, researchers, and technologists in design and development (co-design, iterative feedback loops), rather than purely top-down development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect the realities of classrooms
rubrics_metrics.description: Build open, research-driven technology that reflects the realities of classrooms and strengthens teaching and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions must be context-aware and practical: they should fit teacher workflows, classroom constraints, and real-world implementation conditions rather than being theoretically optimal only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources should be rigorous, connected, and designed to accelerate field progress
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re supporting resources that are rigorous, connected, and designed to accelerate progress across the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect rigor in research and evaluation, interoperability/connectedness across systems or resources, and an orientation toward accelerating large-scale improvement across education rather than isolated pilots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-design with teachers and translational focus to classroom practice
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ve built products and tech platforms for and with teachers — grounded in research that guides how kids learn best — to translate those insights into classroom practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for projects that partner with teachers during development and explicitly translate research findings into usable classroom tools, supports, or curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edtech accuracy, standards alignment, and learning-science backing
rubrics_metrics.description: Edtech products for the public good that are more accurate, aligned with state academic standards, and backed by learning science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation criteria include validity/accuracy of tools, alignment to relevant academic standards, and explicit grounding or validation in contemporary learning science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthy, privacy- and security-conscious AI for education
rubrics_metrics.description: Building Trust in AI for Education (story title) and organizational roles such as Product Management Director, Privacy and Security signal a focus on trustworthy AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects involving AI should address trustworthiness, transparency, privacy, and security; demonstrate safeguards, responsible design, and alignment with ethical/privacy standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewed focus on scaling what works in education
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning Commons builds on over a decade of CZI’s extensive investment and progress, with a renewed focus on scaling what works in education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for initiatives with clear plans and evidence for scale-up, including mechanisms for broad dissemination, adoption, and sustained impact beyond small-scale pilots.
